one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-04. (1) The 8-K/A with pro forma RemainCo financials is due by Oct 7 (EDGAR shows none filed as of Oct 6, src 27); it should firm up post-close net debt and corporate cost, informational. (2) Q2 FY27 earnings: date not yet announced (no notice found on Oct 6), but last year's Q2 call was Oct 29, 2025, so it very likely lands ~Oct 26-29 inside the window. It brings the first continuing-ops FY27 guide and the test of DC margin recovery from 14.8% (management expects 'more favorable margin comparisons beginning in Q2', src 24); Q1's report produced a ~-20% week, so the jump is two-sided and large. (3) Hyperscaler Q3 calls in late October with first 2027 capex guides (mild positive). The Nov 18 Analyst & Investor Day (src 26) is just outside the window but anticipation may support the stock into it. Post-spin selling (stock fell 11.5% on the Sep 28 record date, src 28) looks largely done. No edge on the earnings direction, so I keep a near-symmetric spread around today's price: median ~$183.5, monthly sigma ~21% (71%/3.5 plus an earnings jump), essentially unchanged from round 1.

reasoning: Round 2. Valued only the remaining Climate Solutions company. I accepted and verified three supervisor findings against primary filings: (a) Q1 FY27 corporate & eliminations was -$23.0M in one quarter (src 23), so my round-1 -$40M/yr was too light; I now use -$80M to -$85M; (b) the 10-K says one global technology customer was ~11% of consolidated FY26 sales and top-10 were 49% (src 25), which I use instead of leak-based shares; (c) the Nov 18 Investor Day exists (src 26) and the Q2 report is unannounced but very likely ~Oct 26-29. I also verified the Q1 slides' DC 'earnings growth in excess of 85%' guide (src 24) and stay ~$27M below it (judgment after the Q1 margin miss). Net debt: verified $432.9M at Jun-30 and the $156M distribution; the Gentherm 8-K confirms a separate Cash Transfer was funded (src 30) but not its size, so ~$280M at close is an estimate; with Q1 FCF -$5M and $150-200M capex I cut 12-month FCF to ~$120M (net debt ~$160M at horizon). Peers: dropped Daikin and Munters (different fiscal/consensus basis; Daikin's 7.7x was a basis artifact), leaving 10 peers on one formula: medians 17.9x EV/EBITDA and 27.6x P/E; I withdrew the round-1 premium and apply a ~5% discount for contractually persistent concentration. Result: EBITDA FY27/28/29 $462M/$625M/$734M, NTM at horizon $680M; EV/EBITDA $211 and P/E $213, fair value $212 (from $230); scenario mean ~$215. Alt-lane evidence: Hunterbrook leak still used only as bull-case colour; plant hiring/capacity trackers (src 13, 15, 29) confirm the build-out is real; the 11.5% Sep 28 record-date drop (src 28) looks like spin mechanics. Because execution has missed twice and the market capitalises ~18x my near-term EBITDA, I shade the ladder median to ~$196 (about halfway from $183 to fair value), lognormal sigma ~0.52 with a slightly fatter left tail and a thinner right tail than round 1 (P>=320 0.155 vs 0.205; P>=457 0.04 vs 0.065), consistent with a bull case that needs ~21x on ~$820M. Research limits: sec.gov blocked direct downloads (filings read via WebFetch; EDGAR JSON index fetched directly); X/Reddit not reachable via search. Lane share fell further (~40%) because the supervisor's findings required primary-filing verification.
